paragraphs.text: A new argument of great weight, taken from the example of Abraham the father of all believers: and this is the proposition: if Abraham is considered in himself by his works, he has deserved nothing with which to rejoice with God.
paragraphs.anchor: shall we then say that Abraham

paragraphs.text: By works, as is evident from the next verse.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: A preventing of an objection. Abraham may well rejoice and extol himself among men, but not with God.
paragraphs.anchor: For if Abraham were justified by

paragraphs.text: A confirmation of the proposition: Abraham was justified by imputation of faith, and therefore freely, without any regard being give to his works.

The first proof of the confirmation, taken from opposites: to him who deserves anything by his labour, the wages are not counted as favour, but as debt: but to him that has done nothing but believe in him who freely promises, faith is imputed.
To him that has deserved anything from his work.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: Is not reckoned or given to him.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: That makes him who is wicked in himself to be just in Christ.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: Another proof of the same confirmation: David puts blessedness as a part of the free pardon of sins, and therefore justification also.
paragraphs.anchor: Even as David also describeth the

paragraphs.text: A new proposition: that this manner of justification belongs both to uncircumcised and also to the circumcised, as is declared in the person of Abraham.
This saying of David, in which he pronounces them as blessed.
paragraphs.label: e
paragraphs.anchor: blessedness then upon the circumcision only

paragraphs.text: He proves that it belongs to the uncircumcised (for there was no doubt of the circumcised) in this way: Abraham was justified in uncircumcision, therefore this justification belongs also to the uncircumcised. Nay, it does not belong to the circumcised, in respect of the circumcision, much less are the uncircumcised shut out from it because of their uncircumcision.
A preventing of an objection: why then was Abraham circumcised, if he was already justified? That the gift of righteousness (he says) might be confirmed in him.
Circumcision, which is a sign: as we say the "ordinance of baptism", for "baptism", which is a ordinance.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: Circumcision was previously called a sign, with respect to the outward ceremony. Now Paul shows the force and substance of that sign. That is, to what end it is used, that is, not only to signify, but also to seal up the righteousness of faith. By this we come to possess Christ himself: for the Holy Spirit works that inwardly indeed, which the ordinances being joined with the word, represent.
paragraphs.label: g
paragraphs.anchor: seal of the righteousness of the

paragraphs.text: An applying of the example of Abraham to the uncircumcised believers, whose father he also makes Abraham.
paragraphs.anchor: that he might be the father

paragraphs.text: An applying of the same example to the circumcised believers, whose father is Abraham, but yet by faith.
paragraphs.anchor: And the father of circumcision to

paragraphs.text: A reason why the seed of Abraham is to be considered to be by faith, because Abraham himself through faith was made partaker of the promise by which he was made the father of all nations.
That all the nations of the world should be his children: or by the "world" may be understood the land of Canaan.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: For works that he had done, or upon this condition, that he should fulfil the Law.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: A double confirmation of that reason: the one is that the promise cannot be apprehended by the law, and that if it could it would be made of no effect: the other, that the condition of faith would be joined in vain to the promise if it could be apprehended by works.
paragraphs.anchor: For if they which are of

paragraphs.text: If they are heirs who have fulfilled the law.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: A reason of the first confirmation, why the promise cannot be apprehended by the law: because the law does not reconcile God and us, but rather proclaims his anger against us, because no man can fully keep it.

The conclusion of this argument: the salvation and justification of the posterity of Abraham (that is, of the Church which is composed of all believers) proceeds from faith which lays hold on the promise made to Abraham, and which promise Abraham himself first of all laid hold on.
To all the believers.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: That is to say, not only of those who believe and are also circumcised according to the law, but of those also who without circumcision and with respect of faith only, are counted among the children of Abraham.
paragraphs.anchor: not to that only which is

paragraphs.text: This fatherhood is spiritual, depending only upon the power of God, who made the promise.
Before God, that is by membership in his spiritual family, which has a place before God, and makes us acceptable to God.
paragraphs.label: m

paragraphs.text: Who restores to life.
paragraphs.label: n

paragraphs.text: With whom those things are already, which as yet are not indeed, as he can with a word make what he wishes out of nothing.
paragraphs.label: o

paragraphs.text: A description of true faith wholly resting in the power of God, and his good will, set forth in the example of Abraham.
paragraphs.anchor: Who against hope believed in hope

paragraphs.text: Very strong and steadfast.
paragraphs.label: p

paragraphs.text: Void of strength, and unfit to have children.
paragraphs.label: q

paragraphs.text: Acknowledged and praised God, as most gracious and true.
paragraphs.label: r

paragraphs.text: A description of true faith.
paragraphs.label: s

paragraphs.text: The rule of justification is always the same, both in Abraham, and in all the faithful: that is to say, faith in God, who after there was made a full satisfaction for our sins in Christ our mediator, raised him from the dead, that we also being justified, might be saved in him.
paragraphs.anchor: Now it was not written for

paragraphs.text: To pay the ransom for our sins.
